message.content:
Second independent check. Is this M12 code-review finding a REAL, actionable bug/issue that should be fixed before merge? Read the code yourself. Be skeptical — confirm only if you can point to the concrete problem in the diff.

Lens: money
File: app/(customer)/account/page.tsx (upcoming list filter (line ~77-78) + components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx cancel button (lines 84-100))
Title: In-progress bookings render a Cancel button that always fails
Detail: The account page builds `upcoming` from bookings with status `confirmed` OR `in_progress` and passes them to UpcomingBookings. UpcomingItem carries no status, so UpcomingBookings renders a Cancel button for every item including in-progress sessions. cancelBooking guards `status !== 'confirmed'` and returns `{ok:false, error:'This booking can't be cancelled.'}`, so an in-progress cancel just surfaces an error toast. No money is mis-handled (the server guard correctly refuses), but offering a Cancel/Reschedule action that can never succeed for an active session is a UX defect on the M12 dashboard.

content.text: `in_progress` is a real booking status. Let me confirm it's actually settable on a booking (a booking transitions to `in_progress` when joined) so that an `in_progress` booking truly reaches the `upcoming` list.

Confirmed. When a customer joins a session, the booking status is set to `in_progress` (line 83). That booking then matches the `upcoming` filter (`confirmed` OR `in_progress`), gets passed to `UpcomingBookings`, which unconditionally renders a Cancel button (and a Reschedule button). The `cancelBooking` server action guards `status !== "confirmed"` (line 71), returning `{ ok: false, error: "This booking can't be cancelled." }` — so the cancel always fails with an error toast for in-progress bookings. The same is true for reschedule (line 138 requires `status === "confirmed"`).

All the claims in the finding check out:
- `app/(customer)/account/page.tsx:59-60` — `upcoming` includes both `confirmed` and `in_progress`.
- `components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx:15-20` — `UpcomingItem` carries no status field.
- `components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx:93-100` — Cancel button rendered for every item.
- `app/(customer)/account/actions.ts:71-73` — server guard refuses non-confirmed, returns the exact error quoted.

The finding's characterization is accurate and honest: no money is mis-handled (the server guard correctly refuses capture/refund), so the "money" lens turns up no financial bug. It is a genuine UX defect — an actionable control that can never succeed for active sessions. This is real and fixable (e.g., thread the status through and hide Cancel/Reschedule for `in_progress`).

Confirmed against the diff. account/page.tsx:59-60 builds `upcoming` from bookings with status `confirmed` OR `in_progress`. When a customer joins a session, session/actions.ts:83 sets the booking to `in_progress`, so such bookings really do reach the upcoming list. UpcomingItem (UpcomingBookings.tsx:15-20) carries no status, and UpcomingBookings.tsx:93-100 unconditionally renders the Cancel button (plus Reschedule at 84-92) for every item. cancelBooking guards `if (booking.status !== "confirmed")` and returns `{ok:false, error:"This booking can't be cancelled."}` (actions.ts:71-73), and rescheduleBooking's update is scoped to `.eq("status","confirmed")` (actions.ts:138), so both actions silently fail for in-progress sessions and surface an error toast.

The finding is honest about its own lens: under the "money" lens there is NO financial bug — the server correctly refuses, so no capture/refund is mishandled. What remains is a genuine, concrete UX defect on the M12 dashboard: an actionable Cancel/Reschedule control that can never succeed for an active session. It is real and easily fixable (thread booking status into UpcomingItem and hide/disable Cancel and Reschedule when status === 'in_progress'). Actionable and worth fixing before merge.
